# PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION] Contents of this Part

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION] Title | Number

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION] Procedure for disputing the court’s jurisdiction | Rule 11

## Procedure for disputing the court’s jurisdiction

## 11

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (1) A defendant who wishes to –

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (a) dispute the court’s jurisdiction to try the claim; or

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (b) argue that the court should not exercise its jurisdiction

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] may apply to the court for an order declaring that it has no such jurisdiction or should not exercise any jurisdiction which it may have.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (2) A defendant who wishes to make such an application must first file an acknowledgment of service in accordance with Part 10.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (3) A defendant who files an acknowledgment of service does not, by doing so, lose any right that he may have to dispute the court’s jurisdiction.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (4) An application under this rule must –

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (a) be made within 14 days after filing an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (b) be supported by evidence.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (5) If the defendant –

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (a) files an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (b) does not make such an application within the period specified in paragraph (4),

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] he is to be treated as having accepted that the court has jurisdiction to try the claim.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (6) An order containing a declaration that the court has no jurisdiction or will not exercise its jurisdiction may also make further provision including –

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (a) setting aside the claim form;

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (b) setting aside service of the claim form;

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (c) discharging any order made before the claim was commenced or before the claim form was served; and

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (d) staying (GL) the proceedings.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (7) If on an application under this rule the court does not make a declaration –

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (a) the acknowledgment of service shall cease to have effect;

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (b) the defendant may file a further acknowledgment of service within 14 days or such other period as the court may direct; and

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (c) the court shall give directions as to the filing and service of the defence in a claim under Part 7 or the filing of evidence in a claim under Part 8 in the event that a further acknowledgment of service is filed.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (8) If the defendant files a further acknowledgment of service in accordance with paragraph (7)(b) he shall be treated as having accepted that the court has jurisdiction to try the claim.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (9) If a defendant makes an application under this rule, he must file and serve his written evidence in support with the application notice, but he need not before the hearing of the application file –

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (a) in a Part 7 claim, a defence; or

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (b) in a Part 8 claim, any other written evidence.

[PART 11 – DISPUTING THE COURT’S JURISDICTION > 11] (10) Omitted
